metric.label: Lexical baseline
metric.description: Character n-gram cosine distance. This is a reproducible lexical baseline, not a semantic or faithfulness score.

units.leftText: This is the word of the LORD that came to Joel son of Pethuel:
units.rightText: The word of Jehovah that came to Joel the son of Pethuel.

units.leftText: Hear this, O elders; and give ear, all who dwell in the land. Has anything like this ever happened in your days or in the days of your fathers?
units.rightText: Hear this, ye old men, and give ear, all ye inhabitants of the land. Hath this been in your days, or in the days of your fathers?

units.leftText: Tell it to your children; let your children tell it to their children, and their children to the next generation.
units.rightText: Tell ye your children of it, and let your children tell their children, and their children another generation.

units.leftText: What the devouring locust has left, the swarming locust has eaten; what the swarming locust has left, the young locust has eaten; and what the young locust has left, the destroying locust has eaten.
units.rightText: That which the palmer-worm hath left hath the locust eaten; and that which the locust hath left hath the canker-worm eaten; and that which the canker-worm hath left hath the caterpillar eaten.
leftNotes: 1:4 The precise identification of the four kinds of locusts mentioned here is uncertain.

units.leftText: Wake up, you drunkards, and weep; wail, all you drinkers of wine, because of the sweet wine, for it has been cut off from your mouth.
units.rightText: Awake, ye drunkards, and weep; and wail, all ye drinkers of wine, because of the sweet wine; for it is cut off from your mouth.

units.leftText: For a nation has invaded My land, powerful and without number; its teeth are the teeth of a lion, and its fangs are the fangs of a lioness.
units.rightText: For a nation is come up upon my land, strong, and without number; his teeth are the teeth of a lion, and he hath the jaw-teeth of a lioness.

units.leftText: It has laid waste My grapevine and splintered My fig tree. It has stripped off the bark and thrown it away; the branches have turned white. A Call to Mourning
units.rightText: He hath laid my vine waste, and barked my fig-tree: he hath made it clean bare, and cast it away; the branches thereof are made white.

units.leftText: Wail like a virgin dressed in sackcloth, grieving for the husband of her youth.
units.rightText: Lament like a virgin girded with sackcloth for the husband of her youth.

units.leftText: Grain and drink offerings have been cut off from the house of the LORD; the priests are in mourning, those who minister before the LORD.
units.rightText: The meal-offering and the drink-offering are cut off from the house of Jehovah; the priests, Jehovah’s ministers, mourn.

units.leftText: The field is ruined; the land mourns. For the grain is destroyed, the new wine is dried up, and the oil fails.
units.rightText: The field is laid waste, the land mourneth; for the grain is destroyed, the new wine is dried up, the oil languisheth.

units.leftText: Be dismayed, O farmers, wail, O vinedressers, over the wheat and barley, because the harvest of the field has perished.
units.rightText: Be confounded, O ye husbandmen, wail, O ye vinedressers, for the wheat and for the barley; for the harvest of the field is perished.

units.leftText: The grapevine is dried up, and the fig tree is withered; the pomegranate, palm, and apple— all the trees of the orchard— are withered. Surely the joy of mankind has dried up. A Call to Repentance (Amos 5:4–15|AMO 5:4-15*; Zephaniah 2:1–3|ZEP 2:1-3*; Luke 13:1–5|LUK 13:1-5*)
units.rightText: The vine is withered, and the fig-tree languisheth; the pomegranate-tree, the palm-tree also, and the apple-tree, even all the trees of the field are withered: for joy is withered away from the sons of men.

units.leftText: Put on sackcloth and lament, O priests; wail, O ministers of the altar. Come, spend the night in sackcloth, O ministers of my God, because the grain and drink offerings are withheld from the house of your God.
units.rightText: Gird yourselves with sackcloth, and lament, ye priests; wail, ye ministers of the altar; come, lie all night in sackcloth, ye ministers of my God: for the meal-offering and the drink-offering are withholden from the house of your God.

units.leftText: Consecrate a fast; proclaim a solemn assembly! Gather the elders and all the residents of the land to the house of the LORD your God, and cry out to the LORD.
units.rightText: Sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly, gather the old men and all the inhabitants of the land unto the house of Jehovah your God, and cry unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: Alas for the day! For the Day of the LORD is near, and it will come as destruction from the Almighty.
units.rightText: Alas for the day! for the day of Jehovah is at hand, and as destruction from the Almighty shall it come.

units.leftText: Has not the food been cut off before our very eyes — joy and gladness from the house of our God?
units.rightText: Is not the food cut off before our eyes, yea, joy and gladness from the house of our God?

units.leftText: The seeds lie shriveled beneath the clods; the storehouses are in ruins; the granaries are broken down, for the grain has withered away.
units.rightText: The seeds rot under their clods; the garners are laid desolate, the barns are broken down; for the grain is withered.

units.leftText: How the cattle groan! The herds wander in confusion because they have no pasture. Even the flocks of sheep are suffering.
units.rightText: How do the beasts groan! the herds of cattle are perplexed, because they have no pasture; yea, the flocks of sheep are made desolate.

units.leftText: To You, O LORD, I call, for fire has consumed the open pastures and flames have scorched all the trees of the field.
units.rightText: O Jehovah, to thee do I cry; for the fire hath devoured the pastures of the wilderness, and the flame hath burned all the trees of the field.

units.leftText: Even the beasts of the field pant for You, for the streams of water have dried up, and fire has consumed the open pastures.
units.rightText: Yea, the beasts of the field pant unto thee; for the water brooks are dried up, and the fire hath devoured the pastures of the wilderness.

units.leftText: Blow the ram’s horn in Zion; sound the alarm on My holy mountain! Let all who dwell in the land tremble, for the Day of the LORD is coming; indeed, it is near—
units.rightText: Blow ye the trumpet in Zion, and sound an alarm in my holy mountain; let all the inhabitants of the land tremble: for the day of Jehovah cometh, for it is nigh at hand;

units.leftText: a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and blackness. Like the dawn overspreading the mountains a great and strong army appears, such as never was of old, nor will ever be in ages to come.
units.rightText: a day of darkness and gloominess, a day of clouds and thick darkness, as the dawn spread upon the mountains; a great people and a strong; there hath not been ever the like, neither shall be any more after them, even to the years of many generations.

units.leftText: Before them a fire devours, and behind them a flame scorches. The land before them is like the Garden of Eden, but behind them, it is like a desert wasteland — surely nothing will escape them.
units.rightText: A fire devoureth before them; and behind them a flame burneth: the land is as the garden of Eden before them, and behind them a desolate wilderness; yea, and none hath escaped them.

units.leftText: Their appearance is like that of horses, and they gallop like swift steeds.
units.rightText: The appearance of them is as the appearance of horses; and as horsemen, so do they run.
leftNotes: 2:4 Or like charioteers or like cavalry

units.leftText: With a sound like that of chariots they bound over the mountaintops, like the crackling of fire consuming stubble, like a mighty army deployed for battle.
units.rightText: Like the noise of chariots on the tops of the mountains do they leap, like the noise of a flame of fire that devoureth the stubble, as a strong people set in battle array.

units.leftText: Nations writhe in horror before them; every face turns pale.
units.rightText: At their presence the peoples are in anguish; all faces are waxed pale.

units.leftText: They charge like mighty men; they scale the walls like men of war. Each one marches in formation, not swerving from the course.
units.rightText: They run like mighty men; they climb the wall like men of war; and they march every one on his ways, and they break not their ranks.

units.leftText: They do not jostle one another; each proceeds in his path. They burst through the defenses, never breaking ranks.
units.rightText: Neither doth one thrust another; they march every one in his path; and they burst through the weapons, and break not off their course.

units.leftText: They storm the city; they run along the wall; they climb into houses, entering through windows like thieves.
units.rightText: They leap upon the city; they run upon the wall; they climb up into the houses; they enter in at the windows like a thief.

units.leftText: Before them the earth quakes; the heavens tremble. The sun and moon grow dark, and the stars lose their brightness.
units.rightText: The earth quaketh before them; the heavens tremble; the sun and the moon are darkened, and the stars withdraw their shining.

units.leftText: The LORD raises His voice in the presence of His army. Indeed, His camp is very large, for mighty are those who obey His command. For the Day of the LORD is great and very dreadful. Who can endure it? Return with All Your Heart
units.rightText: And Jehovah uttereth his voice before his army; for his camp is very great; for he is strong that executeth his word; for the day of Jehovah is great and very terrible; and who can abide it?

units.leftText: “Yet even now,” declares the LORD, “return to Me with all your heart, with fasting, weeping, and mourning.”
units.rightText: Yet even now, saith Jehovah, turn ye unto me with all your heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning:

units.leftText: So rend your hearts and not your garments, and return to the LORD your God. For He is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion. And He relents from sending disaster.
units.rightText: and rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto Jehovah your God; for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in lovingkindness, and repenteth him of the evil.
leftNotes: 2:13 Forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

units.leftText: Who knows? He may turn and relent and leave a blessing behind Him — grain and drink offerings for the LORD your God.
units.rightText: Who knoweth whether he will not turn and repent, and leave a blessing behind him, even a meal-offering and a drink-offering unto Jehovah your God?

units.leftText: Blow the ram’s horn in Zion, consecrate a fast, proclaim a sacred assembly.
units.rightText: Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly;

units.leftText: Gather the people, sanctify the congregation, assemble the aged, gather the children, even those nursing at the breast. Let the bridegroom leave his room, and the bride her chamber.
units.rightText: gather the people, sanctify the assembly, assemble the old men, gather the children, and those that suck the breasts; let the bridegroom go forth from his chamber, and the bride out of her closet.

units.leftText: Let the priests who minister before the LORD weep between the portico and the altar, saying, “Spare Your people, O LORD, and do not make Your heritage a reproach, an object of scorn among the nations. Why should they say among the peoples, ‘Where is their God?’” Restoration Promised
units.rightText: Let the priests, the ministers of Jehovah, weep between the porch and the altar, and let them say, Spare thy people, O Jehovah, and give not thy heritage to reproach, that the nations should rule over them: wherefore should they say among the peoples, Where is their God?

units.leftText: Then the LORD became jealous for His land, and He spared His people.
units.rightText: Then was Jehovah jealous for his land, and had pity on his people.

units.leftText: And the LORD answered His people: “Behold, I will send you grain, new wine, and oil, and by them you will be satisfied. I will never again make you a reproach among the nations.
units.rightText: And Jehovah answered and said unto his people, Behold, I will send you grain, and new wine, and oil, and ye shall be satisfied therewith; and I will no more make you a reproach among the nations;

units.leftText: The northern army I will drive away from you, banishing it to a barren and desolate land, its front ranks into the Eastern Sea, and its rear guard into the Western Sea. And its stench will rise; its foul odor will ascend. For He has done great things.
units.rightText: but I will remove far off from you the northern army, and will drive it into a land barren and desolate, its forepart into the eastern sea, and its hinder part into the western sea; and its stench shall come up, and its ill savor shall come up, because it hath done great things.
leftNotes: 2:20 That is, the Mediterranean Sea, also called the Great Sea

units.leftText: Do not be afraid, O land; rejoice and be glad, for the LORD has done great things.
units.rightText: Fear not, O land, be glad and rejoice; for Jehovah hath done great things.

units.leftText: Do not be afraid, O beasts of the field, for the open pastures have turned green, the trees bear their fruit, and the fig tree and vine yield their best.
units.rightText: Be not afraid, ye beasts of the field; for the pastures of the wilderness do spring, for the tree beareth its fruit, the fig-tree and the vine do yield their strength.

units.leftText: Be glad, O children of Zion, and rejoice in the LORD your God, for He has given you the autumn rains for your vindication. He sends you showers, both autumn and spring rains, as before.
units.rightText: Be glad then, ye children of Zion, and rejoice in Jehovah your God; for he giveth you the former rain in just measure, and he causeth to come down for you the rain, the former rain and the latter rain, in the first month.

units.leftText: The threshing floors will be full of grain, and the vats will overflow with new wine and oil.
units.rightText: And the floors shall be full of wheat, and the vats shall overflow with new wine and oil.

units.leftText: I will repay you for the years eaten by locusts — the swarming locust, the young locust, the destroying locust, and the devouring locust — My great army that I sent against you.
units.rightText: And I will restore to you the years that the locust hath eaten, the canker-worm, and the caterpillar, and the palmer-worm, my great army which I sent among you.
leftNotes: 2:25 The precise identification of the four kinds of insects mentioned here is uncertain.

units.leftText: You will have plenty to eat, until you are satisfied. You will praise the name of the LORD your God, who has worked wonders for you. My people will never again be put to shame.
units.rightText: And ye shall eat in plenty and be satisfied, and shall praise the name of Jehovah your God, that hath dealt wondrously with you; and my people shall never be put to shame.

units.leftText: Then you will know that I am present in Israel and that I am the LORD your God, and there is no other. My people will never again be put to shame. I Will Pour Out My Spirit (Acts 2:14–36|ACT 2:14-36*)
units.rightText: And ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am Jehovah your God, and there is none else; and my people shall never be put to shame.

units.leftText: And afterward, I will pour out My Spirit on all people. Your sons and daughters will prophesy, your old men will dream dreams, your young men will see visions.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions:

units.leftText: Even on My menservants and maidservants, I will pour out My Spirit in those days.
units.rightText: and also upon the servants and upon the handmaids in those days will I pour out my Spirit.

units.leftText: I will show wonders in the heavens and on the earth, blood and fire and columns of smoke.
units.rightText: And I will show wonders in the heavens and in the earth: blood, and fire, and pillars of smoke.

units.leftText: The sun will be turned to darkness and the moon to blood before the coming of the great and awesome Day of the LORD.
units.rightText: The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and terrible day of Jehovah cometh.

units.leftText: And everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will be saved; for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be deliverance, as the LORD has promised, among the remnant called by the LORD.[’’]
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of Jehovah shall be delivered; for in mount Zion and in Jerusalem there shall be those that escape, as Jehovah hath said, and among the remnant those whom Jehovah doth call.

units.leftText: “Yes, in those days and at that time, when I restore Judah and Jerusalem from captivity,
units.rightText: For, behold, in those days, and in that time, when I shall bring back the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem,
leftNotes: 3:1 Or restore the fortunes of Judah and Jerusalem

units.leftText: I will gather all the nations and bring them down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. There I will enter into judgment against them concerning My people, My inheritance, Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations as they divided up My land.
units.rightText: I will gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat; and I will execute judgment upon them there for my people and for my heritage Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations: and they have parted my land,
leftNotes: 3:2 Jehoshaphat means the LORD judges; also in verse 12.

units.leftText: They cast lots for My people; they bartered a boy for a prostitute and sold a girl for wine to drink.
units.rightText: and have cast lots for my people, and have given a boy for a harlot, and sold a girl for wine, that they may drink.

units.leftText: Now what do you have against Me, O Tyre, Sidon, and all the regions of Philistia? Are you rendering against Me a recompense? If you retaliate against Me, I will swiftly and speedily return your recompense upon your heads.
units.rightText: Yea, and what are ye to me, O Tyre, and Sidon, and all the regions of Philistia? will ye render me a recompense? and if ye recompense me, swiftly and speedily will I return your recompense upon your own head.

units.leftText: For you took My silver and gold and carried off My finest treasures to your temples.
units.rightText: Forasmuch as ye have taken my silver and my gold, and have carried into your temples my goodly precious things,

units.leftText: You sold the people of Judah and Jerusalem to the Greeks, to send them far from their homeland.
units.rightText: and have sold the children of Judah and the children of Jerusalem unto the sons of the Grecians, that ye may remove them far from their border;
leftNotes: 3:6 Or to the peoples of Javan

units.leftText: Behold, I will rouse them from the places to which you sold them; I will return your recompense upon your heads.
units.rightText: behold, I will stir them up out of the place whither ye have sold them, and will return your recompense upon your own head;

units.leftText: I will sell your sons and daughters into the hands of the people of Judah, and they will sell them to the Sabeans — to a distant nation.” Indeed, the LORD has spoken.
units.rightText: and I will sell your sons and your daughters into the hand of the children of Judah, and they shall sell them to the men of Sheba, to a nation far off: for Jehovah hath spoken it.

units.leftText: Proclaim this among the nations: “Prepare for war; rouse the mighty men; let all the men of war advance and attack!
units.rightText: Proclaim ye this among the nations; prepare war; stir up the mighty men; let all the men of war draw near, let them come up.

units.leftText: Beat your plowshares into swords and your pruning hooks into spears. Let the weak say, ‘I am strong!’
units.rightText: Beat your plowshares into swords, and your pruning-hooks into spears: let the weak say, I am strong.

units.leftText: Come quickly, all you surrounding nations, and gather yourselves. Bring down Your mighty ones, O LORD.
units.rightText: Haste ye, and come, all ye nations round about, and gather yourselves together: thither cause thy mighty ones to come down, O Jehovah.

units.leftText: Let the nations be roused and advance to the Valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I will sit down to judge all the nations on every side.
units.rightText: Let the nations bestir themselves, and come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat; for there will I sit to judge all the nations round about.

units.leftText: Swing the sickle, for the harvest is ripe. Come, trample the grapes, for the winepress is full; the wine vats overflow because their wickedness is great.
units.rightText: Put ye in the sickle; for the harvest is ripe: come, tread ye; for the winepress is full, the vats overflow; for their wickedness is great.
leftNotes: 3:13 LXX the harvest has come; see also Mark 4:29|MRK 4:29*.

units.leftText: Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision! For the Day of the LORD is near in the valley of decision.
units.rightText: Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision! for the day of Jehovah is near in the valley of decision.

units.leftText: The sun and moon will grow dark, and the stars will no longer shine.
units.rightText: The sun and the moon are darkened, and the stars withdraw their shining.

units.leftText: The LORD will roar from Zion and raise His voice from Jerusalem; heaven and earth will tremble. But the LORD will be a refuge for His people, a stronghold for the people of Israel. Blessings for God’s People
units.rightText: And Jehovah will roar from Zion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem; and the heavens and the earth shall shake: but Jehovah will be a refuge unto his people, and a stronghold to the children of Israel.

units.leftText: Then you will know that I am the LORD your God, who dwells in Zion, My holy mountain. Jerusalem will be holy, never again to be overrun by foreigners.
units.rightText: So shall ye know that I am Jehovah your God, dwelling in Zion my holy mountain: then shall Jerusalem be holy, and there shall no strangers pass through her any more.

units.leftText: And in that day the mountains will drip with sweet wine, and the hills will flow with milk. All the streams of Judah will run with water, and a spring will flow from the house of the LORD to water the Valley of Acacias.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the mountains shall drop down sweet wine, and the hills shall flow with milk, and all the brooks of Judah shall flow with waters; and a fountain shall come forth from the house of Jehovah, and shall water the valley of Shittim.

units.leftText: Egypt will become desolate, and Edom a desert wasteland, because of the violence done to the people of Judah, in whose land they shed innocent blood.
units.rightText: Egypt shall be a desolation, and Edom shall be a desolate wilderness, for the violence done to the children of Judah, because they have shed innocent blood in their land.

units.leftText: But Judah will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.
units.rightText: But Judah shall abide for ever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.

units.leftText: For I will avenge their blood, which I have not yet avenged. ” For the LORD dwells in Zion.
units.rightText: And I will cleanse their blood, that I have not cleansed: for Jehovah dwelleth in Zion.
leftNotes: 3:21 Or For I will pardon their bloodguilt, which I have not yet pardoned.
